lines.373: Draw near, bow low, and worship --
lines.374: him, cloud-dark, who swallows all seven worlds whole.
lines.375: Hold fast to him -- my heart praises Him who, having torn open
lines.376: that unyielding foe's chest, now dwells in flower-decked Thiruppadagam.
lines.377: He who dwells within my heart, who rests upon my very head;
lines.378: the gem-hued One who tore open the demon's hard chest;
lines.379: the Ancient One who, of old, turned back the very cycles of time itself;
lines.380: the Discus-bearer whom the whole world praises -- he, the Lord of Thiruvathiyur.
lines.381: The Lord of Athiyur, who rides upon the great bird;
lines.382: who sleeps upon the serpent whose hood is set with gleaming, jewel-like spots;
lines.383: who is himself the three sacred fires; and who is Lord even over Him
lines.384: who once drank the poison of the great ocean -- he alone is our own true Master.
lines.385: You are our own Lord, the very chief of the immortal, unblinking gods;
lines.386: O tall, red-eyed Mal, of the sacred, Lakshmi-graced chest;
lines.387: you dwell there, resting upon the rearing, thousand-hooded serpent,
lines.388: and have made Kudamookku your very temple.
lines.389: Taken up and nurtured, he grew as a mere infant;
lines.390: and yet he is the same One who once swallowed all seven worlds, drawing them within himself.
lines.391: Here, as the cowherd boy, dancing with pots upon his hands, he came and settled --
lines.392: the Lord who has made my very own heart his dwelling place.
lines.393: 'O Lord, our own Master, grant us your grace!' -- so saying,
lines.394: the celestials stood in due order and showered clustered flowers upon him.
lines.395: And he -- of resounding anklets on his red feet, the tall, red-eyed One --
lines.396: in the form of a dwarf, then in that vast form, took the earth for his own. He is Mal.
lines.397: O Mal! O towering One! O Krishna! O you who stand supreme
lines.398: even above the celestials, wearer of the wondrous tulsi garland!
lines.399: O you who once, that day, brought down the wood-apple fruit with a hurled calf --
lines.400: my love for you knows no bounds at all!
